git add -A && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
Root the eventtap against the GC — deleting _whisper silently killed the trigger

_whisper was removed as dead state because its `recording` field was never
updated. It was not dead: `_whisper.modTap = modTap` was the only strong reference
to the trigger eventtap. Hammerspoon collects eventtaps, repeating timers and
watchers that nothing in Lua references, and collecting one unregisters it from
the system — no error, no log line, isEnabled() true right up to the collection.

init.lua's top-level locals are not a root: after the chunk returns a local lives
only while a reachable closure captures it, and the only closure holding modTap
was the 5s watchdog timer, whose own handle was discarded. So the whole chain was
collectible, and the trigger worked for a couple of minutes after each reload and
then went dead — the press produced nothing at all, not even the overlay.

Long-lived objects now live in a LocalWhisper table: the tap, its watchdog, and
the sleep watcher (which had the same problem and would have quietly stopped
recovering dictations interrupted by sleep).

The suite gains a `lifetime` group: no top-level constructor may discard its
result, and every top-level local holding an eventtap/watcher/repeating timer must
be stored into the root table. Stripping the root from the current file fails all
three checks. Verified live by forcing two full GC cycles and posting a synthetic
press — the tap still answers. 75 checks pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
git log --oneline -1
